Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching our Q3 embeddings rate card (PDF) with baseline public tiers and a shortlist of recommended models. Short answers up front: 

- Billing: embeddings are billed per-vector (not per-token) for the hosted embeddings endpoint. Where tokenization matters (e.g., models that generate embeddings from text with internal chunking), we normalize to a single vector output per request when the model is configured for single-vector embeddings.

- Dimensions: our public rate card lists unit prices for the common sizes (128/256/512/1024). We also support custom-dimension vectors (charged at the closest higher published bucket).

- Models: our catalog supports embeddings for the Redwood-embed-* family and several community models we host. The rate card includes recommended models for high-recall search (balanced cost/quality): Redwood-embed-large-512, Redwood-embed-512-quant, and two open variants we host.

- Discounts/Packages: we offer committed-volume tiers (monthly/annual) and a dedicated "embeddings-only" bundle for high-volume retrieval use cases. Committed tiers are applied as a % off the public per-vector rate and can be combined with reserved capacity for SLA.

I pasted the key excerpt from the attached PDF below for quick reference. Let me know if you want a worked example for 3M vectors at 256 dims.

Attachment: redwood-embeddings-ratecard-2026Q3.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

Subject: Re: Embeddings pricing — technical notes on dims & models

Hi all — jumping in with the technical clarifications that often help procurement and engineering teams align: 

1) Per-vector semantics: when we say "per-vector" we mean one paid unit per returned vector. If you request multiple vectors (e.g., one per chunk or multiple pooling strategies), each returned vector counts. For standard single-vector endpoints billed as embeddings.generate we count 1 unit per response vector.

2) Dimensions and buckets: public buckets in the rate card are 128, 256, 512, and 1024. If you request a non-standard dimension (e.g., 300), we map to the next published bucket (in that example, 512) for pricing and to maintain compatibility with our vector store optimizations.

3) Tokenization edge cases: some text inputs are internally chunked before embedding (long documents). We provide an optional batching utility that will re-assemble chunked vectors for charging visibility; by default each chunk -> vector maps to a unit. We can enable a fixed "document -> consolidated vector" mode for a POC if you prefer a different billing approach, but that requires a small engineering toggle and usually sits behind a committed-tier discussion.

4) Model differences: Redwood-embed-large-512 and the quantized variants produce higher-quality vectors for search but cost more per unit. Open variants are cheaper but may need more vectors (different chunking) to reach parity on recall; factor that into cost comparisons.

Happy to run a quick calculator — if you can share an approximate average document length and the expected chunking policy we can produce an apples-to-apples cost estimate.

— Karthik

Subject: Re: Embeddings pricing — commercial proposal and next steps

Hi Olivia — thanks for the specific asks. Quick commercial proposal below and next steps to get you pricing in procurement-ready format.

Summary (worked examples attached):
- Public list: $0.00025 / vector at 256 dims (Redwood-embed-256 bucket)
- No-commit monthly (3M vectors): $750.
- 12-month commit (36M vectors/year): we can offer a 12% committed discount off the public list for a 12-month volume commitment at 36M vectors/year. This nets approximately $0.00022/vector -> ~$660/month equivalent.
- Reserved capacity + burst: for predictable latency and SLA, reserved capacity pricing combines a monthly reservation fee (covers baseline throughput) + a reduced per-vector rate for committed usage; e.g., $X/month reservation + $0.00020/vector for committed units. Exact reservation fee depends on required throughput and concurrency — we can size this after a short telemetry call.
- Large-commit band: for multi-year commitments >=50M vectors/year we can discuss up to 15–20% discounts and bespoke packaging (e.g., dedicated pools, data isolation).
- Onboarding: one-time ingestion & POC support fee is typically a small professional services line (we've quoted $6k–$12k historically depending on connector scope; we can waive part of this on larger commits).
- Billing: yes — we can provide separate line items for embeddings vs generation in invoices. We also support metered usage exports and token/vector-level CSVs for reconciliation.

Attachments: QTM-8731-initial-quote.pdf (PDF, 45KB), redwood-embeddings-ratecard-2026Q3.pdf

Next steps: 
1) I can drop a procurement-ready quote (DocuSign) with the 12% committed example for 36M vectors/year.
2) If you want reserved capacity sizing, our capacity team will run a short (30–45 min) call to collect concurrency and latency targets.
3) We'll set up a POC scope doc (SOW) if you want to validate model quality; Karthik's team can help with evaluation prompts & metrics.

Would you like me to send the DocuSign with the 12% committed example?
